rules.effective_date_basis: These laws, described below, took effect on January 1, 2026.
rules.title: Ban on collusive or coercive use of common pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Businesses, including apartment rental companies, may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of an agreement to restrain trade. They also may not use or offer a common pricing algorithm to coerce users to adopt the algorithm’s pricing or commercial-term recommendations in California.
rules.key_value: Common pricing algorithm with two or more users using competitor data

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies to users and distributors of common pricing algorithms; a pricing algorithm is common if it has two or more users and uses competitor data in setting pricing or commercial terms.
coverage.summary: Applies statewide to businesses using, distributing, selling, licensing, or otherwise providing access to common pricing algorithms, including but not limited to apartment rental companies.

rules.exemptions: The document states that single-firm proprietary algorithms using only the business’s own data are not covered.
rules.penalty: The amendments introduce civil fines of up to $1 million in cases brought by the Attorney General or a district attorney, and increase criminal fines to the greater of up to $6 million or twice the gain or loss for corporations and the greater of up to $1 million or twice the gain or loss for individuals.
rules.interaction: The document states that fines under the Cartwright Act are cumulative to each other and to those imposed under other state statutes.
rules.quoted_span: Businesses are expressly prohibited from using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade. Defendants will argue that this does not really expand the scope of liability, but additional scrutiny and legal arguments by claimants seem inevitable.
